The three small fixes (theme-color, Go omitempty and the Go view-name check) came back committed but unchecked. Nothing ran on WSL before it went down. I've queued all three to be checked on the Mac and landed on develop together, after the safe-HTML binding and then the loop/select and navigation-hang fixes.

The Mac check covers formatting, the full lint, each fix's own tests including the Go and TinyGo runtime tests, the website content check and the repository policy, all on the merged code. A fix lands only if all of that passes. The Mac's single heavy-job slot is still held by another session's release check, so nothing new is on develop yet.

What each fix does:
- **Go view names:** a Go page that reads a service member with the wrong capitalisation, like `oauthNotice` for `oAuthNotice`, now fails to build with a "did you mean" message instead of silently showing nothing. It only catches case slips, and only for Go services.
- **Go omitempty:** Go services now follow standard Go JSON tags (`omitempty`, `omitzero`, `string`, `-`) when sending data.
  - This changes behaviour: a required-field check now rejects an empty string on an `omitempty` field.
  - The same encoding also writes query values, cache keys and stored entities.
- **Theme colour:** a `theme_color` in the web app manifest now adds the matching `<meta name="theme-color">` tag to every page.

The route-budget branch and the inbox-shaped navigation-hang test both still need the Windows machine, so they wait until it is working again.
